news_feature.weighting: Equal publisher mean; recency half-life 14 days; other-state-only articles receive 0.25 relevance. Party direction clips D tone minus R tone to [-1,1]; a missing counterpart contributes zero, not an imputed observation.
news_feature.limitation: RSS affect and local outcome rules are observational news features. They do not measure voter opinion or establish demographic response.

population_coverage.ethnicity_bridge: Observed C15002H White non-Hispanic and C15002I Hispanic; nonwhite Hispanics allocated proportionally among B-G within sex and education. Total A-G population conserved.

limitations: Experimental two-party forecast. Win probabilities use historical error widths and have not been backtested.
ACS counts are residents age 25+, including noncitizens, weighted by CES validated turnout by race, sex and education. Voters age 18-24 are absent.
2024 CES v10 uses pre-election survey weights because post-wave weights and validated votes are unavailable in this cached release.

The national environment is half the average out-party midterm gain (four midterms) and half the generic-ballot average. The group news coefficient is fitted to ten group-midterm observations and is imprecise.
Nonwhite Hispanic populations are allocated proportionally within sex and education; that race/ethnicity bridge is estimated, not an observed intersection.
House geography uses ACS 119th-Congress district proxies; 2026 redistricting has not been reconciled.
Candidate identity, incumbency, campaign spending, differential turnout, third parties, and election-specific uncertainty are not modeled.
Senate and governor baselines share fitted state preferences with House and add 2024 national office effects; they do not transfer a past candidate's personal vote.
projection.message: 2024 cohort baselines anchored to the actual 2024 presidential result, reweighted to the expected midterm electorate, shifted by the national environment (half typical out-party midterm gain, half generic-ballot polls) and by learned group news effects, then combined by expected voters. Win probability = Phi(margin / sigma).
